name: comfort
description: Being within a tolerable zone of physical, social, or mental expectations such that there are no pressing desires to improve the immediate situation.
perceptions: There's nothing annoying me physically, no unusual anxiety, no particular social pressures.

comparisons.description: 'Satisfaction' is a limited sensation that something specific meets your expectations, while 'comfort' is a generalized sense that there's nothing that needs to be improved right now. For instance, you could be satisfied that you did a good job gluing the handle back on the mug, but still have mental discomfort about something else going on in your life. If you manage to obtain a state of mental comfort, you're currently satisfied about everything considered important.

variations.name: social comfort
variations.description: The immediate social situation doesn't include any significant negative perceptions or require special attention to stay in the tolerable zone.
perceptions: At the moment, things are fine socially.
I'm amongst people who respect and accept me as part of the group.
I don't have to strive for acceptance.

variations.name: physical comfort
variations.description: A perception that your body is not experiencing any significant negative sensations. In the modern world, we tend to take comfort for granted.
perceptions: I'm healthy, it's not too hot, not too cold, the chair is comfy, all is well.

variations.name: mental comfort
variations.description: A perception that your mind is not experiencing any significant negative sensations or strong desires.
perceptions: I'm not particularly anxious about anything.
I'm doing things that are aligned with my goals and preferences.
examples: doing a favorite puzzle to pass time

commentaries.quote: 'Comfort' is relative. Most of us are never truly without some kind of discomfort for long, but some people have higher tolerances physical or social discomfort.
You can be physically comfortable while being mentally uncomfortable or vice versa. In fact, for many of us in the modern world, they're almost always out of sync by definition.
Art should comfort the disturbed and disturb the comfortable.
We find comfort among those who agree with us - growth among those who don't.
